extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for inventorship, corrective actions (supplemental oaths/declarations, substitute statements), applicant identity, and related procedural formalities under 35 U.S.C. and 37 C.F.R. as set out in the MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint inventorship under 35 U.S.C. 116
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 116 (and 37 CFR 1.45) allows inventors to apply for a patent jointly even though (A) they did not physically work together or at the same time, (B) each did not make the same type or amount of contribution, or (C) each did not make a contribution to the subject matter of every claim of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2109.01 for discussion of legal requirements. When an application is filed with joint inventors, the examiner should assume that the subject matter of various claims was commonly owned at the time the inventions were made unless evidence indicates otherwise. Multiple inventors named in an application must have made a contribution, individually or jointly, to at least one claim (nonprovisional) or to the subject matter disclosed (provisional).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship when claims change (37 CFR 1.48)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are responsible for correcting, and are required to correct, the inventorship in compliance with 37 CFR 1.48 when the application is amended to change the claims so that one (or more) of the named inventors is no longer an inventor of the subject matter of a claim remaining in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests under 37 CFR 1.48 filed on or after September 16, 2012 are treated by OPAP; if granted, OPAP will correct Office records and send a corrected filing receipt. Examiners should remind applicants of the necessity to correct inventorship when restriction/election leads to cancellation of claims of an inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single invention requirement and restriction practice (35 U.S.C. 121)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be directed to only a single invention (35 U.S.C. 121). If an application by joint inventors includes more than one independent and distinct invention, restriction may be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restriction may result in the need to change inventorship if the elected invention was not the invention of all originally named inventors. A divisional application complying with 35 U.S.C. 120 would be entitled to the benefit of the earlier filing date. Examiner should remind applicants to correct inventorship pursuant to 37 CFR 1.48 if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner approach to inventorship and invention dates
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should not inquire of the patent applicant concerning the inventors and the invention dates for the subject matter of the various claims until it becomes necessary to do so in order to properly examine the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume common ownership of the subject matter of various claims in joint-inventor applications unless evidence to the contrary exists. The USPTO or a court may inquire of inventorship or ownership when necessary (see 37 CFR 1.110).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding claims to inventions by inventors not named (amendment permitted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending nonprovisional applications will be permitted to be amended by complying with 37 CFR 1.48 to add claims to inventions by inventors not named when the application was filed as long as such inventions were disclosed in the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.48 permits correction of inventorship where the correct inventor(s) were not named in an application for patent. The amendment cannot introduce new matter; added claims must be supported in the original disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental oath or declaration (37 CFR 1.67) — post‑Sept 16, 2012
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.67 allows the applicant to submit an inventor's oath or declaration meeting the requirements of § 1.63, § 1.64, or § 1.162 to correct deficiencies or inaccuracies present in an earlier-filed inventor's oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deficiencies due to failure to meet § 1.63(b) may be corrected with an application data sheet under § 1.76, except corrections of inventorship must be pursuant to § 1.48. A supplemental inventor's oath or declaration must be executed by the person whose oath/declaration is being withdrawn, replaced, or otherwise corrected. The Office will not require additional oaths if original complied with 35 U.S.C. 115 and § 1.63 or 1.162.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter via supplemental oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: No new matter may be introduced into a nonprovisional application after its filing date even if an inventor's oath or declaration is filed to correct deficiencies or inaccuracies present in the earlier-filed oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental oaths/declarations cannot be used as vehicles to add disclosures; applicants should bear in mind that supplemental filings cannot introduce new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA supplemental oath/declaration rules (pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.67)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.67 allowed the Office to require, or inventors/applicants to submit, a supplemental oath or declaration meeting the requirements of § 1.63 or § 1.162 to correct deficiencies or inaccuracies in an earlier-filed oath or declaration, and specified who must sign depending on whether the deficiency related to all inventors or fewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (1) citizenship error of one inventor may be corrected by that inventor alone; (2) omission of duty-to-disclose clause requires signatures of all inventors; (3) mailing address errors may be corrected by a supplemental declaration signed by the affected inventor or by an ADS under § 1.76. If an inventor refuses or cannot be found, signature requirement may be suspended or waived under § 1.183; available joint inventors must sign on behalf of themselves and the nonsigning inventor where appropriate (see MPEP § 409.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental oath or declaration filed after allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental oaths and declarations covering the claims in the application may be filed after allowance as a matter of right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When received they will be placed in the file by the Office of Data Management but their receipt will not be acknowledged. They should not be filed or considered as amendments under 37 CFR 1.312 since they make no change in the wording of the papers on file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute statements in lieu of oath/declaration (37 CFR 1.64) — scope
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.64 permits an applicant under § 1.43, 1.45 or 1.46 to execute a substitute statement in lieu of an oath or declaration under § 1.63 if the inventor is deceased, is under a legal incapacity, has refused to execute the oath or declaration under § 1.63, or cannot be found or reached after diligent effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision applies to applications filed on or after September 16, 2012 and implements 35 U.S.C. 115(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute statement content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute statement must: (1) comply with § 1.63(a) identifying the inventor(s) and stating upon information and belief the facts the inventor is required to state; (2) identify the person executing the substitute statement and their relationship to the inventor and provide residence/mailing address unless supplied in an ADS; (3) identify the circumstances permitting execution (deceased, incapacitated, refused, cannot be found); and (4) unless in ADS, identify each inventor by legal name and last known mailing address and residence where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For nonprovisional international design applications, the requirement to identify residence/mailing address is satisfied by presentation of such information prior to international registration. The substitute statement must contain an acknowledgment of criminal penalties for willful false statements (18 U.S.C. 1001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Person executing substitute statement must review and understand application
rubrics_metrics.description: A person may not execute a substitute statement for an application unless that person has reviewed and understands the contents of the application, including the claims, and is aware of the duty to disclose to the Office all information known to the person to be material to patentability as defined in § 1.56.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although a non-inventor applicant is not required to submit proof of the permitted circumstance, the signer must have reviewed the application; proof of attempts to secure the inventor's signature should be kept in the applicant's file when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may execute a substitute statement (permitted applicant entities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitted entities to execute a substitute statement include: (i) the inventor’s legal representative under 37 CFR 1.43 (if deceased or incapacitated), (ii) other joint inventors under 37 CFR 1.45 (if the inventor refuses or cannot be found), (iii) an applicant under 37 CFR 1.46 who is the assignee or party to whom the inventor is obligated to assign, and (iv) an applicant under 37 CFR 1.46 who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where multiple assignees or obligated assignees together are the applicant, all such parties must execute the substitute statement on behalf of the non-signing inventor. Example: if Company X and Company Y together are applicant, both must execute the substitute statement and neither may act alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee/juristic entity substitute statement requirements and signature authority
rubrics_metrics.description: When an assignee or juristic entity executes a substitute statement, the assignee must supply residence and mailing address (for juristic entity, use entity address), include applicant name and the title of the person executing the statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a juristic entity, the substitute statement may be signed by a person with apparent authority (e.g., an officer) or by any person if the statement sets forth that the signer is authorized to act on behalf of the entity (e.g., general counsel). A power of attorney to a patent practitioner does not make that practitioner an official of the juristic entity or empower the practitioner to sign the substitute statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to submit proof of permitted circumstance (but keep records)
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-inventor applicant need not submit proof of the permitted circumstance (e.g., death certificate) to file a substitute statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the permitted circumstance is other than death or legal incapacity, the inventor must have refused to execute the oath or the applicant must have exercised diligent effort to find or reach the inventor. Proof of attempts to secure the inventor's signature should be kept in applicant's files even though not submitted to the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'applicant' (37 CFR 1.42)
rubrics_metrics.description: The word 'applicant' refers to the inventor or all joint inventors, or to the person applying for a patent as provided in §§ 1.43, 1.45, or 1.46. If a person is applying under § 1.46, the word refers to the assignee, the person to whom the inventor is under an obligation to assign, or the person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fewer than all joint inventors are applying under § 1.45, 'the applicant' means the joint inventors applying without the omitted inventor(s). Any person having authority may deliver application and fees on behalf of the applicant, but oaths/declarations/substitute statements, correspondence addresses, and signatures are governed by specific rules (§§ 1.63/1.64, 1.33(a), 1.33(b)). The Office may require additional information where ownership or interest is in question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications by legal representative and joint inventors (37 CFR 1.43 and 1.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an inventor is deceased or under legal incapacity, the legal representative may make an application on behalf of the inventor (37 CFR 1.43). Joint inventors must apply jointly and each must make the inventor's oath or declaration as required by § 1.63, except as provided for in § 1.64 (37 CFR 1.45).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a joint inventor refuses or cannot be found after diligent effort, the other joint inventors may make the application on behalf of themselves and the omitted inventor; see § 1.64 for substitute statements in such cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application by assignee/party with proprietary interest (37 CFR 1.46) — ADS and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A person to whom the inventor has assigned or is under an obligation to assign, or a person showing sufficient proprietary interest, may make an application under 37 CFR 1.46; such applications must contain an application data sheet under § 1.76 specifying applicant information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant is assignee or obligated assignee, documentary evidence of ownership (assignment, employment agreement) should be recorded no later than issue fee payment. If applicant is a person otherwise showing proprietary interest, submit a petition with fee (§ 1.17(g)), a showing of sufficient proprietary interest, and a statement that making the application as agent is appropriate to preserve rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction or change of applicant name and post‑filing change of applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request to correct or update the name of the applicant must include an application data sheet under § 1.76 specifying the correct or updated name. Any request to change the applicant after an original applicant has been specified must include an ADS and comply with §§ 3.71 and 3.73.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A change in the name of applicant recorded pursuant to Hague Agreement Article 16(1)(ii) will be effective to change the name in a nonprovisional international design application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath/declaration execution and patent grant to real party in interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if whole or part interest is assigned, an oath or declaration must be executed by the actual inventor(s) except as provided in § 1.64. If a patent is granted on an application filed under § 1.46 by a person other than the inventor, the patent shall be granted to the real party in interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a real party in interest has filed under § 1.46, the applicant must notify the Office of any change in the real party in interest no later than payment of the issue fee; the Office will treat absence of notice as indication of no change. The Office may publish notice of filing by a person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest in the Official Gazette.
